objectives.text: Keep the ruling family in control and the succession orderly by governing without the National Assembly: the Emir dissolved parliament on 15 Feb 2024, suspended it and seven articles of the 1962 constitution on 10 May 2024 for up to four years (a restoration window to May 2028), and the Emir and the government now exercise legislative power by decree. The citizenship campaign (a December 2024 law allowing revocation for 'moral turpitude' or acts threatening state security; about 42,000 revoked in six months by March 2025, at least 50,000 by December 2025 on Middle East Eye's count, campaigners say up to 200,000) is part of the same project: narrowing the body of citizens who share the welfare state.

grand_strategy.reading:
Kuwait is a small rich state whose strategy has been, since 1961, to buy
protection with money and mediation and to keep every neighbour a little in debt
to it. 2024-2026 broke the model on two fronts at once. At home the Emir ended
the one thing that distinguished Kuwait in the Gulf, an elected assembly with
real vetoes: he governs by decree, passed the debt law that the Assembly had
blocked, and used the nationality law as a welfare and political instrument. Abroad
the 2026 war with Iran turned the host of the largest US ground presence in the
region into the Gulf state that is struck most often: the guarantor from 1991
could not stop Iranian drones, and the 'we allowed no use of our land' line is
as much a plea to Tehran as a statement of fact. The paradox that runs
through the card is that every protection Kuwait buys has a price in exposure:
the US bases invite attack, the Chinese-built port on Bubiyan invites Iraqi and
Iranian pressure, the decree rule that unlocked the money costs it the
institutions that absorb shocks, and the extra partners (Pakistan, India, the UK)
add cover, not guarantees. Two signals that are not rows: the Emir's description
of Iran as a 'friend' even while it attacks, which keeps a way back open, and the
absence of any Kuwaiti step toward Israel when its neighbours debate it.
Questions for the next pass: the outcome of Iraq's Federal Supreme Court on the
Khor Abdullah appeal (hearings were postponed to mid-June 2025), Kuwait's own
reaction to the June 2025 Israel-Iran war, the current status of the Durra
negotiations, and the Kuwait-China oil trade, which this pass could not source.

stances.note: Stable de facto alignment since the 1991 liberation: Kuwait was designated a major non-NATO ally in 2004, hosts the main US ground presence in the region (Camp Arifjan, Camp Buehring, Ali Al Salem, Port Shuaiba) and AGSI writes that no other power can replace Washington as its primary security guarantor. No mutual-defence treaty text was verified in this pass, so the grade rests on the designation and the de facto presence. Friction is real and rising, hence cooling: friendly fire downed three US F-15Es on 2 Mar 2026, six US soldiers died at Port Shuaiba on 1 Mar, Kuwait diversifies (Pakistan, India, UK) and insists it allowed no use of its land, airspace or waters against Iran. Bond - affinity: the 1991 legacy, gratitude and a shared interest.
